This vignette explains the date-aware split of candidate patches added in
OtsuFire 2.1.0: the problem it solves, the rule, the recommended way to apply
it to years that were already processed, and its main limitation.

## The problem: patches that mix haze and fire

The summer change-index composite is built pixel by pixel from the available
post-event images. Band 2 of the mosaic, `DOY_post`, records the day of year of
the image that supplied each pixel. In a year with persistent haze, smoke or
cloud residue, pixels of a haze-affected date can touch pixels of a real fire
observed weeks earlier or later. Otsu-guided growth then joins them into a
**single candidate**, and the classifier scores the whole mixture as one
object. If the mixture looks burned enough, the haze is accepted together with
the fire and the commission error rises.

## The rule

`split_patches_by_doy()` reads the DOY of the pixels inside each candidate of
at least 50 ha and groups them:

1. Pixels with the same DOY form an initial group.
2. Groups with fewer than `max(10, 5 %)` of the pixels are absorbed into the
   group with the closest median DOY.
3. The two groups with the closest **medians** are merged while their medians
   differ by `doy_gap_days` or less. The default is **30 days**.
4. A candidate with two or more remaining groups is *mixed*. It is replaced by
   one sub-patch per connected component of each group (components below nine
   pixels are dropped).

Candidates with a single group are untouched, so a year without date mixtures
changes very little.

## Recommended use: update a year that is already processed

The deterministic stage is slow and its results are already published, so the
recommended flow does **not** repeat it. `run_split_rescore()` takes the scored
candidates that already exist, splits the mixed ones, extracts the predictors of
the sub-patches, scores them with the model and recipe you give it (no
retraining) and writes the final map:

```{r}
library(OtsuFire)

res <- run_split_rescore(
  year                 = 2006L,
  scored_candidates    = "Results/2006/SUPERVISED/FINAL_MAPS/POOL_GLOBAL_SUPPL/SCORE/2006_deterministic_scored.gpkg",
  change_index         = "Imagery/Min_Min/MinMin_2006_mosaic_res90m.tif",
  delayed_change_index = "Imagery/Autumn/mean_mean_2006_mosaic.tif",
  topo                 = "Topography/elevation_slope.tif",
  corine_raster        = "Corine_Masks/CLC_2006_peninsula.tif",
  model                = "FINAL/final_model.rds",
  recipe               = "FINAL/recipe.rds",
  threshold            = 0.51,
  out_dir              = "Results_v2.1/2006",
  doy_gap_days         = 30
)

res$audit               # parents split, sub-patches, patches kept before/after
res$thresholded_path    # binary map to validate with validate_fire_maps()
```

Next to the maps the run writes `RECIPE.yml` (package commit, every parameter,
input paths, model training parameters) and `sessionInfo.txt`, so each year can
be reproduced and compared with the original.

Validate the new map with the same protocol as the original one, changing only
the input map:

```{r}
validation <- validate_fire_maps(
  input_shapefile = res$thresholded_path,
  ref_shapefile   = "Fires/Validation_fires_burneable_verano_FINAL/Effis_CA_2006_maskKeep_summer.gpkg",
  mask_shapefile  = "mask.gpkg",
  burnable_raster = "Corine_Masks/burneable_mask_binary_corine06_wgs84.tif",
  year_target     = 2006L,
  validation_dir  = "Results_v2.1/2006/VALIDATION"
)
```

## Another route, not validated

`refine_params = list(split_by_doy = TRUE, doy_gap_days = 30)` in
`build_burned_mapping_config()` runs the same split inside
`run_deterministic_pipeline()`, between detection and scoring. Deterministic
filters would then see the sub-patches and the result would not match maps
already published. This route is off by default and has only been tested with
synthetic data; use `run_split_rescore()` to update years.

## What to expect

Validation against the official perimeters, original map against G = 30:

| Year | Reference | F1 original | F1 split |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2006 | EFFIS | 0.441 | 0.672 |
| 1986 | Neves atlas + regional | 0.625 | 0.635 |
| 1992 | Neves atlas + regional | 0.459 | 0.483 |
| 2017 | EFFIS | 0.780 | 0.778 |

2006 is the year with the most haze: commission falls from 0.70 to 0.43 while
omission barely moves (0.17 to 0.18).

## Limitation: years without haze

In 2017, a year without a haze problem, the split is not free. Of 301 split
parents in the original map, 215 improve but 77 get worse, and the F1 changes
by -0.002 overall (-0.003 in Spain and in Portugal). The losses come from small
sub-patches (about 100 pixels or less) at the edge of real fires: the fire was
observed on dates more than 30 days apart, the split separates its edge, and the
classifier scores the small piece below the threshold. Smaller gaps lose more:
with `doy_gap_days = 15` the 2017 F1 fell by 0.007.

Practical consequences:

* A gap of 30 days is a compromise, not an optimum. Do not tune it per year
  without an independent reference.
* The scoring model was trained on whole patches. Sub-patches have different
  area and dispersion, so the model is applied slightly outside its training
  distribution.
* Topography dispersion of very small sub-patches moves in the second
  decimal of the score with the cropped window; this does not change the
  conclusions.
